title: Wrapper correctly defangs DeepBook's internal min-out check by passing 0 — single-gate design verified
description: The wrapper invokes `pool::swap_exact_base_for_quote(pool, base_in, deep_in, 0, clock, ctx)` with literal `0` as DeepBook's `min_quote_out`. DeepBook's own assertion at pool.move:412-414 (`assert!(quote_out.value() >= min_out, EMinimumQuantityOutNotMet)` where `EMinimumQuantityOutNotMet: u64 = 12`) therefore can never fire on this path. The wrapper's own `assert!(coin::value(&quote_out) >= min_out, EInsufficientOutput)` is the sole slippage gate, so a slippage-floor breach always produces `EInsufficientOutput` and never DeepBook's code 12. T-002's `expected_failure(abort_code = ::slippage_swap::slippage_swap::EInsufficientOutput)` validates this gate-ownership invariant — the test would fail if DeepBook's check fired first. Synthesis-notes calls this design choice out explicitly. Correct.
impact: Confirms the contract.md AC2.3 promise that EInsufficientOutput is the documented, single, stable abort code for slippage-floor breaches. E-002's CLI assertion has a deterministic target.
recommendation: None. Add a brief Move comment on line 44 noting DeepBook's `EMinimumQuantityOutNotMet = 12` exists and is intentionally bypassed, so a future maintainer doesn't 'helpfully' forward `min_out` into DeepBook and inadvertently make slippage failures abort with code 12 instead of 0.

title: EInsufficientOutput = 0 collides with seven other DeepBook error codes also valued 0 — bare-numeric CLI capture is ambiguous
description: The wrapper picks `const EInsufficientOutput: u64 = 0;`. DeepBook's bundled package itself uses error code `0` in at least seven other modules: `state::history::EHistoricVolumesNotFound`, `balance_manager::EInvalidOwner`, `book::order::EInvalidNewQuantity`, `book::order_info::EOrderInvalidPrice`, `helper::big_vector::ESliceTooSmall`, `helper::constants::EOrderInfoMismatch`, `helper::math::EInvalidPrecision`. Move's `expected_failure(abort_code = ::slippage_swap::slippage_swap::EInsufficientOutput)` qualifies the abort by full module path, so T-002 distinguishes correctly. The on-chain CLI consumer (E-002) assertion, however, frequently captures only the numeric `abort_code` (a u64) plus the abort module address; if a downstream test or operator asserts on the bare `0` and the swap path happens to hit, e.g., `helper::big_vector::ESliceTooSmall` for an unrelated reason during the same tx, both conditions look identical at the CLI surface level. Pool-level `EInvalidQuantityIn` is `6`, `EMinimumQuantityOutNotMet` is `12` (these don't collide with 0), but the helper-module collisions are real. The convention in DeepBook's own pool.move is to start error codes at `1` precisely to leave `0` as 'unused / sentinel'.
impact: E-002's CLI capture (per spec) asserts on the abort code as a stability anchor across slot 2's CI signal. A bare-numeric collision means an unrelated DeepBook-helper abort during a slippage-failure capture could falsely satisfy the assertion (or, conversely, a real slippage failure could be confused for a helper bug). The qualified-module form (`abort_module = slippage_swap::slippage_swap`, `abort_code = 0`) eliminates ambiguity, but only if E-002 captures both; the contract.md doesn't pin which it does.
recommendation: Two options, choose one: (a) Renumber `EInsufficientOutput` to a non-zero constant unique within the wrapper's likely callstack (e.g., `1001` — DeepBook's own error codes range 0-20). This is one line change and a tests.json amendment to T-002's `abort_code = ::slippage_swap::slippage_swap::EInsufficientOutput` constant reference (which is symbolic, so no test edit needed if the test references the constant by name). (b) Leave the value at 0 but require E-002 to capture and assert on the *qualified* abort source `(abort_module, abort_code)` tuple — document this as a hard expectation in contract.md so a CLI-only consumer cannot rely on the bare numeric. Option (a) is more robust; the contract.md text already says 'documented error code' but doesn't mandate the qualified form.

title: DeepBook's silent early-return on lot-size rounding produces quote_out=0 → wrapper aborts with EInsufficientOutput, conflating two distinct failure modes
description: DeepBook's `swap_exact_quantity` (called via `swap_exact_base_for_quote`) at pool.move:384-387 contains a silent early-return path: `base_quantity = base_quantity - base_quantity % self.load_inner().book.lot_size(); if (base_quantity < self.load_inner().book.min_size()) { return (base_in, quote_in, deep_in) };`. When the caller passes a `base_in` whose value, after lot-size rounding, falls below the pool's `min_size`, DeepBook returns the ORIGINAL coins unchanged — meaning `quote_out` is the zero-value `coin::zero(ctx)` constructed at line 256 (the wrapper passes no quote_in; DeepBook synthesizes one). The wrapper's `assert!(coin::value(&quote_out) >= min_out, EInsufficientOutput)` then aborts with `EInsufficientOutput` for any caller-supplied `min_out > 0`. Operator sees 'slippage floor not met' when the actual root cause is 'input below pool min_size after lot-size rounding'. Two materially different failure modes — caller-side input sizing bug vs. genuine adverse market impact — produce identical abort signatures. Neither T-001/T-002/T-004/T-005 exercises this lot-size boundary; the test fixture's `1 * float_scaling()` base_in is comfortably above the test pool's min_size.
impact: Operator debugging E-002 in the wild can't tell from the abort code alone whether to (a) increase input size (b) widen slippage tolerance (c) suspect a stale price oracle. Worse: T-004 (`min_out = 0`) would silently SUCCEED in this lot-size-rounding-trips early-return scenario — `quote_out.value() = 0 >= 0` — and the user would receive their input coins back unchanged, with no on-chain signal that the swap effectively no-op'd. The DEEP fee residual would also be returned in full. Hidden no-op risk for `min_out = 0` callers.
recommendation: Add a defensive check after the swap call but before the slippage assertion: if `coin::value(&quote_out) == 0 && coin::value(&base_residual) == coin::value_pre_swap` (capture pre-swap base value), abort with a distinct `ESwapNoOp: u64 = 1` (or similar). Even simpler: assert `coin::value(&quote_out) > 0` for the `min_out > 0` case before the `>= min_out` check, so a no-op path produces a separable error. Alternatively document this conflation in the doc-comment so E-002's failure-triage runbook tells operators to inspect base_residual when EInsufficientOutput fires.

title: Wrapper does not pre-validate base_in.value() > 0 — zero-value input falls through to DeepBook's EInvalidQuantityIn=6, not the wrapper's documented error vocabulary
description: Contract.md line 4-5 says the caller supplies 'a Coin<BaseAsset> of size > 0', but the wrapper does not enforce this. A caller passing `base_in` with `value() == 0` reaches DeepBook's `swap_exact_quantity` line 365: `assert!((base_quantity > 0) != (quote_quantity > 0), EInvalidQuantityIn)` — DeepBook synthesizes `quote_in = coin::zero(ctx)` so both `base_quantity == 0` and `quote_quantity == 0`, and the XOR is `(false != false) = false`, triggering abort with `EInvalidQuantityIn: u64 = 6` from `deepbook::pool`. The CLI consumer sees code 6 from a different abort module. The wrapper's documented error vocabulary is exactly one constant (`EInsufficientOutput=0`); other failure modes leak the upstream abort code unmodified, contradicting the synthesis-notes framing of 'wrapper's assert is the gate'.
impact: Calls with malformed input (zero-value base coin, possibly produced by a buggy frontend) abort with a non-wrapper error code that the caller can't trivially map to 'invalid input'. Combined with R3-002, the abort-code surface area for a slippage-swap call is the union of `slippage_swap::EInsufficientOutput=0` AND every error code in DeepBook's pool/balance_manager/book/state/helper modules. Caller-side error handling cannot enumerate these.
recommendation: Add a pre-flight check: `assert!(coin::value(&base_in) > 0, EZeroInput)` with a new constant `const EZeroInput: u64 = 1;`. This shifts the error vocabulary from one to two stable codes, both owned by the wrapper module, making caller-side handling tractable. Optional: also pre-validate `coin::value(&deep_in) > 0` if pool fee_type requires DEEP (per pool config); though DeepBook handles missing-DEEP via `pay_with_deep = deep_in.value() > 0` so a zero DEEP coin is valid for input-fee pools — would need to know which pool variant to know if the assertion is correct.

title: Assertion fires BEFORE transfers — no partial-state risk, no coin leak on abort (correctness verification)
description: Verification: the slippage `assert!` at line 47 fires before any of the three `transfer::public_transfer` calls at lines 51-53. On abort, Move's resource model destroys the entire function frame — `base_residual`, `quote_out`, and `deep_residual` are all owned by the frame at abort point, so they are not orphaned (Move would reject the module at compile time if any owned resource without `drop` were leaked, and `Coin<T>` does not have `drop`). Transaction effects are atomic in Sui: an aborted transaction commits no object writes, so the upstream `pool: &mut Pool<...>` mutations performed by `swap_exact_base_for_quote` (place_market_order, balance manager temp creation/deletion, etc.) are all rolled back at the runtime layer. Net result: a slippage abort produces zero on-chain state delta, and the caller's input `Coin<BaseAsset>` and `Coin<DEEP>` remain owned by the sender as inputs. Correct.
impact: Ensures the spec's 'no state is created, no objects are minted by the wrapper itself' (contract.md line 16-17) holds even on the failure path, not just success. T-005's 'no BalanceManager owned by sender' assertion also implicitly holds on abort (the temp_balance_manager DeepBook constructs at pool.move:389 is rolled back).
recommendation: None — informational. Worth one inline comment near the assert noting 'aborts here roll back the temp balance manager DeepBook constructed' so a reviewer doesn't worry the temp BM leaks into operator's account on failure (it doesn't, by Sui transaction-atomicity).

title: Test suite has no coverage for DeepBook-side aborts — wrapper behaviour under EInvalidQuantityIn / EMinimumQuantityOutNotMet untested
description: T-001 (success), T-002 (slippage abort), T-004 (min_out=0 success), T-005 (success + transfer fan-out + no-BM) all exercise the WRAPPER-side code path. None exercises a DeepBook-side abort to confirm: (a) the wrapper does NOT swallow / re-wrap a DeepBook abort into EInsufficientOutput (it can't, by Move's panic semantics, but that's an unverified assumption); (b) the EInvalidQuantityIn=6 case from a zero-value base coin actually surfaces with abort module = `deepbook::pool` and not the wrapper's module; (c) the lot-size early-return from R3-003 produces the surprising 'EInsufficientOutput when the swap effectively no-op'd' behaviour. Lacking these tests, the contract.md error contract ('the wrapper aborts with the documented error code on floor breach') is not pinned against the alternative ('the wrapper aborts with the documented error code AND ONLY on floor breach').
impact: Future refactor (e.g., someone removes the `min_quote_out = 0` permissive forward in favor of forwarding `min_out` directly to DeepBook) would change the abort code from EInsufficientOutput=0 to EMinimumQuantityOutNotMet=12 for slippage-floor breaches, silently breaking E-002's CLI assertion. T-002 would still pass because of the synthesized `coin::zero` quote being below `min_out` and the wrapper's own assert firing first — except with the refactor it WOULDN'T fire first, and T-002 would catch it. So T-002 actually does catch this regression. Less load-bearing than initially feared, but the lot-size case (R3-003) is genuinely uncovered.
recommendation: Add T-006: pass a base_in whose value is exactly `lot_size - 1` (i.e. less than min_size after rounding); assert the wrapper aborts with EInsufficientOutput when min_out > 0, AND succeeds (with quote_out.value() == 0 returned to sender as a zero-value coin) when min_out = 0. This pins the lot-size-rounding behaviour as documented (whether 'documented' means 'aborted' or 'silent no-op' is a contract-level decision per R3-003). Add T-007: pass `coin::zero<BaseAsset>(ctx)` as base_in; assert abort_code = `::deepbook::pool::EInvalidQuantityIn` (numeric 6) — pins the contract that input-shape errors leak from DeepBook unwrapped (or, if R3-004 is fixed, that the wrapper's own EZeroInput fires).

title: Move 2024 clever-error syntax (#[error] attribute) not used — bare u64 abort code lacks attached human-readable message
description: Per `.move-book-docs/reference/abort-and-assert/clever-errors.md` and `.move-book-docs/book/guides/better-error-handling.md`, Move 2024 supports the `#[error]` attribute on error constants, allowing the constant to hold a human-readable string that surfaces in CLI/explorer abort traces alongside the numeric code. The wrapper uses the legacy form `const EInsufficientOutput: u64 = 0;`. The doc-comment above it is helpful for reading source but does not flow through to the abort surface — a CLI capturing the abort sees only `MoveAbort(MoveLocation { module: ..::slippage_swap, function: 0, instruction: N }, 0)`, no string. The clever-error form would produce a richer trace.
impact: Operator-side debugging of E-002 abort captures has less context than is possible. Minor: the symbolic name is recoverable via source inspection. The contract.md does not REQUIRE the clever-error form — the named-constant + doc-comment form satisfies AC2.3's 'documented, named error code'. Counts as info because adopting clever errors is a Move 2024 best-practice but not contracted.
recommendation:
Optional upgrade for a future iter: ```move
#[error]
const EInsufficientOutput: vector<u8> = b"realised quote output below caller's min_out slippage floor";
```
This still aborts with a stable identifier and adds a string the CLI / explorer can show. Trade-off: changes the abort_code shape (vector<u8> hash vs u64), so re-pin T-002 and any E-002 CLI assertion. Defer to forge-quality reviewer (R-quality) for whether to adopt; flagged here for completeness of the error-handling lens.

title: T-002 hard-codes min_out=1e15 — within u64 range but doesn't probe upper-edge u64::MAX overflow boundary
description: T-002 sets `let min_out: u64 = 1_000_000_000_000_000;` (1e15, ~5.4% of u64::MAX). This is comfortably above any realisable output for `1 * float_scaling()` base input. However, the wrapper's `assert!(coin::value(&quote_out) >= min_out, ...)` involves no arithmetic on `min_out` (no subtraction, no addition, no overflow risk), so an upper-edge value like `u64::MAX` would behave identically. Worth noting that the test as written verifies the assertion fires for a 'large but not maximal' value; an overflow regression in some hypothetical future refactor (e.g. computing `min_out * fee_factor` before comparing) would not be caught by 1e15 specifically.
impact: Negligible. The assertion is a direct `>=` comparison with no arithmetic; any value above realisable suffices to cover today's behaviour. Calling out for completeness only.
recommendation: Consider one of: (a) pin `min_out: u64 = 18_446_744_073_709_551_615` (literal u64::MAX) in T-002 to lock in 'no overflow under the maximum possible caller input'; (b) leave as-is and document tests.json T-002 'behavior' as 'min_out far above realisable, not necessarily u64::MAX'. Both fine; (a) is robustness-positive at zero cost.
evidence: let min_out: u64 = 1_000_000_000_000_000; // far above realisable for 1 base unit

title: T-005 takes the DEEP and base residuals but asserts no value bound — a future bug returning wrong coin type would pass the test
description: T-005's checks for the DEEP residual (`let deep_residual = test.take_from_sender<Coin<DEEP>>(); test.return_to_sender(deep_residual);`) and base residual confirm an object of the expected type exists at the sender, but assert NOTHING about its value. If a future refactor accidentally swapped the order of `transfer::public_transfer` calls (e.g., transferring `quote_out` twice and dropping `deep_residual`), the test framework's `take_from_sender<Coin<DEEP>>()` would abort because no `Coin<DEEP>` is at the sender — but this aborts with a test-framework error, not a clean assertion failure with a meaningful code. The test would fail noisily, but the diagnostic would be 'object not found' rather than 'wrapper failed to forward DEEP residual'. Lower-confidence because the test does ultimately catch the bug, just opaquely.
impact: Diagnostic clarity on regression, not pass/fail correctness. Marginal — the test does catch the bad refactor.
recommendation: Optional: add `assert!(coin::value(&deep_residual) <= DEEP_IN, 6)` as a sanity bound (residual cannot exceed input) and `assert!(coin::value(&base_residual) <= base_in_amount(), 7)` similarly. These are weak invariants but make a future regression's failure message much more pointed.

title: T-003 dropped for legitimate test-fixture reasons — boundary case (value == min_out) is asymptotic, not a real coverage gap
description: Verification that the T-003 drop documented in synthesis-notes and tests.json amendment is acceptable from an error-handling-lens standpoint. The dropped test would have pinned `min_out == realised_output` (the exact-equality boundary on the `>=` operator). Synthesis-notes correctly observes that this boundary is asymptotic between T-001 (succeeds for `value > min_out`) and T-002 (aborts for `value < min_out`); a `>` vs `>=` regression — the only realistic boundary bug — would surface in T-001 (if `>=` flipped to `>`, T-001 would still pass because realised value strictly exceeds min_out=0.5; the regression is silent there) or T-002 (would still abort because realised < 1e15; regression silent there too). Honest assessment: T-003's drop DOES leave a real `>=` vs `>` ambiguity uncovered. The friction note in raw-friction.log (line 29) accurately captures the test-scenario fixture limitation; the workaround would require restructuring the test to do exact-realised-output discovery off-chain (compute the expected output deterministically from float_scaling and pool parameters, then pin min_out to that value in a single test_scenario pair). Not blocking this iteration; flagging as a lingering boundary-coverage gap.
impact: If a future maintainer changes `>=` to `>`, neither T-001 nor T-002 catches it. T-004 (min_out=0) requires `quote_out.value() >= 0` which is trivially true under both `>=` and `>` (assuming u64 semantics — `> 0` requires strict positivity, so a zero-output swap WOULD fail under `>` but pass under `>=`). T-004 partially covers the boundary if quote_out > 0 strictly; but the more direct exact-equality test is missing.
recommendation: Future iter: add T-006 that computes the expected realised output deterministically (the 'simulate then swap' pattern: invoke `pool::get_quantity_out(0, base_quantity, clock)` first, capture the returned `quote_quantity`, then call the wrapper with `min_out = quote_quantity` exactly). This sidesteps the two-scenarios-per-test fixture limitation by using a view function in the same scenario. Defer; not a blocker for cycle-2 ship.
